statement: Targets change only on rows where i0 bid and ask price columns both update.
predicted_observable: zero target changes on rows without a joint i0 price event
falsifier: any target change on a non-event row

statement: Each sequence's targets are integer multiples of one of four quanta {0.12543,0.24133,0.46854,0.65687}, defining market classes with different tick regimes.
falsifier: non-integer multiples or other quanta

statement: Features are rank-Gauss transformed: bounded near +-2.326 (Phi^-1(0.99)) with sentinel -5.19934 = Phi^-1(1e-7) for missing values.
falsifier: values outside that support other than the sentinel

statement: Training the row-clock GRU on all 10,607 sequences for more epochs lifts validation WP well above baseline.
falsifier: gain < 0.02
notes: 1024x1 epoch 0.596 (valid256) vs full x2 epochs 0.596 (valid600); class 3 stays 0.35-0.44.

statement: A Rust per-row GRU kernel is several times faster than onnxruntime for the dense GRU 256x2.
falsifier: < 1.5x speedup
notes: Rust 112 us vs ORT 119 us; all dense kernels 12-15 GFLOPS on this host; FLOP-bound.

statement: Skipping zero input columns in the input projection cuts its cost proportional to density.
notes: 5.6 vs 16.6 us at 1/3 density (microbenchmark, not yet in model).

statement: is_scored is predictable from causal features, so propensity-weighted training aligns the loss with scored rows.
falsifier: AUC < 0.6 or no WP gain
notes: AUC 0.816, top 30% propensity rows hold 72% of scored rows. Weighted training not yet run. E-030 shows the true mask measure helps (+0.029); next: causal propensity weights on train data.

statement: Class-3 targets are a function of recent event-clock book states, so event-lag features fix class 3.
falsifier: metric-true class-3 WP does not improve
notes: Event rows 0.708-0.832 but metric-true 0.017-0.024: long quiet visits dominate scored rows; evaluating on event rows was an artifact.

statement: Class-3 WP is bounded by predictability of the next book-state change during a visit.
predicted_observable: known next state lifts class-3 metric far above snapshot models
notes: next 1 state oracle 0.773, next 4 states 0.871; current state only 0.009.

statement: Snapshot queue/flow features (volumes, depletion since event, trades, i1, a*) predict class-3 break direction throughout the visit.
falsifier: AUC near 0.5 more than ~20 rows before the break
notes: AUC 0.997 at 1 row, 0.83 at 6-20, 0.59 at 21-100, 0.55 at >100; row-weighted visit length 247. Class-3 HGB/linear metric 0.33-0.36.

statement: Online (per-sequence, label-free) transition statistics of book states predict the next break direction early in a visit, lifting class 3.
predicted_observable: break-direction AUC > 0.7 at >20 rows before break with Markov features
falsifier: AUC gain < 0.03 over E-013 features
notes: AUC 21-100 rows 0.605 vs 0.602 snapshot; class-3 WP 0.340 vs 0.351.

statement: Class-3 scored rows concentrate just before breaks, so near-break weighting would lift class 3.
falsifier: scored rows not closer to breaks than unscored rows
notes: Class-3 scored rows are farther from breaks: 57% of |y|-weighted scored rows are >=21 rows away vs 38% of unscored rows. Class 2 shows the opposite pattern.

statement: i1 price moves lead i0 breaks, so i1 moves accumulated since the last i0 break predict break direction far from the break.
falsifier: univariate AUC < 0.55 at 21-1000 rows in class 3
notes: Class 3 best AUC 0.53; class 0 0.58 at 101-1000 rows. Sign-cumsum encoding; a proper cointegration residual on reconstructed levels is not yet tested (H-015).

statement: Class-3 WP is capped near 0.42-0.50 because break direction is only predictable within ~20 rows of a break.
predicted_observable: oracle limited to near-break horizon reproduces model scores
notes: Caveat: E-018 no-future baseline used only current and previous state; E-021 then showed long-memory level deviation adds nothing, so the conclusion stands but the bound is not rigorous. Perfect next-state knowledge within 20 rows gives 0.420, within 100 rows 0.615. With class shares ~25/17/19/38% an overall 0.80 needs classes 0-2 near 1.0 or class-3 direction knowledge ~500 rows ahead.

statement: Targets are future level changes over a horizon on the event clock (t0 ~ future bid - current ask, t1 ~ current bid - future ask), which would make past targets computable online after the horizon.
predicted_observable: exact or near-exact reconstruction of targets from later features
falsifier: reconstruction correlation stays < 0.8 with better level recovery
notes: Class-3 targets are -1/0 quanta with mean ~-1 and corr(t0,t1) ~-0.93, consistent with spread-crossing definitions; sign-cumsum levels reach r 0.5-0.6 at K 8-16 events (classes 0-2) and 1-4 events (class 3). Raw p columns are not levels (r ~0).

statement: Class-3 targets are anchor minus current price with a slow anchor, so a label-free level reconstruction from price jumps and its deviation from an EMA equilibrium predicts targets.
representation_change: rebuild the unobserved price level from L2 differences
causal_mechanism: mean reversion toward a slowly moving fair value
falsifier: class-3 WP < 0.1
notes: Price jumps explain 90% of target-jump variance at class-3 events (bounce), but decoded jump sums score ~0 while true jump sums score 0.82: large target jumps are anchor changes, i.e. future information. The -3/+5 jump in research/visual/02 exceeds the +2 price move.

statement: A 64-byte-aligned weight arena in access order, zero-alloc stepping, folded-normalization sparse input and vectorizable bounded-error activations speed up the per-row GRU by >= 1.5x.
representation_change: treat the step as a cache/branch problem instead of a BLAS problem
causal_mechanism: fewer cache misses, no libm calls, skipped zero columns
falsifier: < 1.2x at hidden 256
notes: 1.15x at hidden 256 (FLOP-bound), 1.25x at 192, 1.46x at 128 with target-cpu=native; portable x86-64-v3 1.11-1.12x. Errors: exact path < 2e-5, approx path < 1e-4 after 300 steps; sigmoid < 2e-6, tanh < 4e-6, GELU < 5e-6.

statement: Training directly on the competition objective (weighted Pearson loss per TBPTT chunk) beats the mixed corr + weighted-MSE loss.
falsifier: pure corr loss scores below mix on dev600
notes: corr 0.294/0.257 vs mix 0.604/0.598 (epochs 0/1). Per-chunk correlation is degenerate when class-3 targets are constant within a 2000-row chunk.

statement: Train and validation differ in market-class mix; matching the validation mix by weighted sampling improves validation WP.
predicted_observable: class-balanced arm > control on dev600, gains in classes 0/1
falsifier: no gain beyond seed noise under paired bootstrap

statement: An event-clock GRU stepping only on i0 price events, alongside the row GRU, carries event-level state across long quiet visits and lifts classes 2-3.
representation_change: two clocks: rows and price events
causal_mechanism: row GRU must hold event information over hundreds of rows; the event GRU sees each price event once
falsifier: paired bootstrap CI includes 0 and class 2/3 unchanged
notes: Causality, chunk invariance and a future-leak mutant are tested (tests/test_dual_clock.py).

statement: Sentinel -5.19934 (missing) values distort per-column normalization; replacing them with a neutral value plus missing flags improves WP.
falsifier: no gain under paired bootstrap

statement: Class experts (or a model trained without class-3 dominance) lift classes 0-2, where headroom exists.
representation_change: partition by causally inferable tick regime
causal_mechanism: 43% class-3 train data pulls shared capacity toward large-tick dynamics while validation is 40% classes 0/1
predicted_observable: classes 0-2 dev WP +0.02 for a class-0-2-only model
falsifier: classes 0-2 within CI of the joint model
cheap_test: train on class 0-2 train sequences, score classes 0-2 on dev with oracle class

statement: The WP-optimal prediction is E[m|y|y|x]/E[m|y||x] with m = is_scored; training with mask x |y| weights beats |y| weights alone.
representation_change: treat the scoring mask as part of the measure, not as evaluation bookkeeping
causal_mechanism: is_scored is predictable from x (AUC 0.82) and may covary with y given x
predicted_observable: devB WP gain of mask-weighted over plain fine-tune on devA
falsifier: paired bootstrap CI includes 0
notes: devB: mask-weighted 0.6306 (seeds 1 and 2) vs plain 0.6012/0.5998; all classes up, class 3 +0.06. Independent audit pending.

statement: Residual decomposition by class x rows-to-break x |y| locates recoverable error in classes 0-2.
cheap_test: per-row weighted residual contributions of the best checkpoint on dev
falsifier: losses spread uniformly with no actionable slice

statement: Validation-period data is closer to test conditions; fine-tuning on devA improves devB more than the same amount of extra train data.
representation_change: treat time period as a domain; online-learning analogue of the Jane Street 8th place
causal_mechanism: class mix and likely dynamics drift between periods (E-024)
predicted_observable: devA fine-tune > train-data continuation > frozen base on devB
falsifier: devA fine-tune within CI of the train-data continuation
notes: devA plain fine-tune 0.6012 vs extra train data 0.6017: classes 0-2 +0.007..0.009, class 3 -0.014.

statement: Auxiliary heads predicting the target 20 and 200 rows ahead (Jane Street multi-responder pattern) regularize the main head.
falsifier: dev600 WP below the mix control
notes: 0.512 vs 0.598; class 2 collapses to 0.39. Far-horizon row-shifted targets in sparse-event classes are mostly unpredictable future anchor changes and their gradients dominate shared capacity.

statement: More recurrent capacity lifts WP; with limited data the gain is only realized with early stopping or more sequences.
notes: h384 epoch0 0.6096 vs h256 0.6036 (+0.006, single seed, not yet bootstrapped); both degrade in epoch 1 on 3000 sequences.

statement: Class-0/1 models under-react to imminent large moves one to a few rows before a price break, where direction is observable; a sharper near-break pathway (event-time features, dual clock, or a dedicated head) recovers that gap.
representation_change: treat the pre-break window as a separate regime
causal_mechanism: row GRU smooths over the short pre-break window; the metric's |y| weights concentrate there in class 0
predicted_observable: class-0 WP +0.03 with gap at rows_to_break=1 shrinking
falsifier: class-0 gap at 1 row unchanged
cheap_test: re-run E-029 decomposition on the dual-clock arm

statement: Tempering propensity weights p^alpha trades bias for variance; alpha != 1 beats alpha = 1.
representation_change: loss as importance-weighted risk under the scoring distribution
causal_mechanism: high-variance weights overfit rare high-propensity rows; low alpha under-focuses
predicted_observable: devB WP differs by >= 0.005 between alpha 0.5/1/2
falsifier: all within 0.003
cheap_test: devA fine-tunes with p^0.5, p^1, p^2

statement: Training from scratch on all train sequences with propensity weights exceeds devA fine-tuning gains.
falsifier: devB WP <= 0.6306
notes: unblocked by excluding corrupt row group 528 (E-035); ab5 chain running.

falsifier: AUC gain < 0.02 with 100 future rows

notes: flags+20 future rows AUC 0.711 vs flags-only 0.674; GRU causal propensity 0.911.
